Welcome to Sancar Lunar Lab!

We are students from Prof. Dr. Aziz Sancar Science High School. For Space Apps 2026, we are building an AI-integrated web platform for the CLPS Lunar Mission.
summary:
We developed ASTROMED, an interactive health tracking and mission readiness platform designed for astronauts during long-duration space missions. The platform brings together physical vital signs, mental health indicators, and spacecraft environment data into one simple dashboard. By using a rotatable 3D human body model, 14-day trend charts, and clear color-coded alerts, ASTROMED helps astronauts easily check their own health status within seconds.

Our project directly addresses the challenge of deep-space communication delays. On long missions to the Moon or Mars, crews cannot always wait for immediate medical advice from Earth. ASTROMED solves this by analyzing key metrics—such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels, and sleep—and warning the crew before small health issues become serious emergencies.

This tool is important because it reduces stress on astronauts, saves critical time, and helps keep the entire crew safe and ready for every mission task.
details:
What Does It Do and How Does It Work? ASTROMED is an autonomous astronaut health tracking and mission readiness platform designed for long-duration space missions. It brings together physical vital signs (such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels, and body temperature), mental health indicators, and spacecraft cabin conditions into one unified dashboard. The platform evaluates incoming data against aerospace safety ranges and displays the results through an interactive 3D rotatable human body model, 14-day trend charts, and clear color-coded alerts. It is organized into four main modules: Main Dashboard, Personal Health Data, Crew & Cognitive, and Mission & Environment, allowing astronauts to check their status and generate instant health reports in seconds.

Benefits and Intended Impact During deep-space missions to the Moon or Mars, communication delays make immediate medical support from Earth impossible. ASTROMED solves this problem by empowering crews to monitor their own health independently. By turning complex medical numbers into simple visual indicators, it saves critical time, reduces mental stress on astronauts, and helps prevent minor health issues from turning into serious emergencies. Furthermore, its modular design makes it adaptable for spacecraft, space stations, lunar bases, and training simulations on Earth.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used We built ASTROMED using modern web technologies—including JavaScript, React, Next.js, and Three.js / WebGL for the interactive 3D body visualization—hosted on a fast cloud web server. Our health parameters and threshold logic were designed using NASA Human Research Program (HRP) guidelines on the five hazards of human spaceflight.

Creativity and Factors Considered Instead of presenting astronauts with hard-to-read tables of numbers, we creatively combined 3D anatomical visualization with color-coded readiness scores so any crew member can understand their health at a glance, even without deep medical training. When designing the platform, our team carefully considered deep-space communication delays, the psychological effects of isolation, high crew workload, offline autonomous usability, and dual-language accessibility (English and Turkish) to ensure an inclusive and practical user experience.
